data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is strictly more fragile than a large service with strict internal redundancy, because small services lack the economic slack to afford non-operational diversity and thus concentrate on the same minimum-cost dependencies.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The large service's internal redundancy is merely logical replication on a single physical substrate","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Operators possess private information leading to genuine substrate divergence","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Regulation forces operator diversity","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service is cost-constrained in the same way","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Independent operators facing similar market pressures converge on identical commodity infrastructure (cloud availability zones, managed databases, core CDNs) because the cost of diverging exceeds the expected loss from a correlated outage. The large service has explicit economic slack to fund internal replication across diverse substrates, whereas small operators each optimize independently and converge to a monoculture.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
